children: The Ibovespa rose about 1% to hover around 185,500 on Wednesday following new election polls indicating a tighter race and softer-than-expected US PCE inflation.
President Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro entered the final days before the presidential election in a technical tie in a likely second round, according to Meio/Ideia and Indexa/Broadcast polls.
The Meio/Ideia poll showed the candidates separated by just 0.5 percentage points in a potential runoff.
Meanwhile, US PCE inflation came in slightly below estimates, easing some concerns over further Fed rate hikes.
In contrast, Brazil’s PPI rose 2.5% year over year in August after increasing 1.9% in July.
Major banks gained, with Itaú up more than 1% and Bradesco and BB rising over 1.5% each.
Utilities also advanced, with Sabesp gaining 2%.
Petrobras rose more than 1% as the oil rally resumed.
Vale rebounded nearly 1% from Tuesday’s losses as Chinese iron ore prices rose.

title: Ibovespa Rises Following Election Polls and US Inflation
